And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri V.K. Pandey - Advocate for the appellants.
 None for the respondents.

Order 
With the consent of both learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 against the award dated 16.12.2004 passed in Claim Case No.55/2004 by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Damoh seeking setting aside of impugned award/reduction of compensation.
Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that in the instant case, at the time of incident, offending vehicle was not moving, it was in stationary condition.
Therefore, present case would not come within the purview of accident arising out of use of motor vehicle.
Further, it is also urged that Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.1,600/- per month, which is excessive.
It should be suitably reduced.
On above grounds, it is urged that appeal filed by appellant be allowed.
Heard and perused record of the case.
So far as first submission of learned counsel for the Insurance- Company is concerned, it is correct that at the time of incident, offending vehicle was not moving and it was in stationary condition.
It is also evident from record of the case that at the time of accident, deceased was working inside offending vehicle and while deceased was working inside offending vehicle, then,
explosion
took place and on account of the same, deceased expired.

In this Court's considered opinion, in view of law laid down in Shivaji Dayanu Patil and Another Vs.
Vatschala Uttam More (Smt.) (1991) 3 SCC 530 and Kalim Khan and Others.

1 Others (2018) 7 SCC 687, present accident would be treated as accident arising out of use of motor vehicle.
So far as income of deceased's is concerned, evidently, at the time of accident, deceased was working as welder.
On the date of accident, minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.2,250/- and minimum wages of semiskilled labour were Rs.2,313/-
Tribunal has determined deceased's monthly income as Rs.1,600/- per month.
Therefore, it cannot be said that income determined by Tribunal is erroneous.
Hence, in view of discussions in the foregoing paras, no ground is made out for interference in the findings recorded by the Tribunal.
Hence, appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.
(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE 3 MA-574-2005 vai United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Manaklal Vishwakarma & Ors.
